title: Accident insurance
summary: Describes UnitedHealthcare branded accident insurance cash-benefit plans, what they cover, why they may matter and key disclosures.

atoms.title: What accident insurance is
atoms.question: What is accident insurance?
atoms.text: Accident insurance is also known as supplemental accident insurance or personal accident insurance. With accident coverage, cash benefits help pay for expenses related to a qualifying accident. UnitedHealthcare says that can include things like ambulance care, physical therapy, lost wages and more.

What is personal accident insurance?
Does accident insurance pay for lost wages?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare accident plans and underwriter
atoms.question: Who offers UnitedHealthcare accident insurance plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare branded accident plans are underwritten by Golden Rule Insurance Company and offer a variety of cash-benefit options. These plans help pay for expenses related to accidental injuries. Plans can be viewed by state using a ZIP code, or by calling 1-866-671-0378.

How do I get an accident insurance quote?

atoms.title: Is accident insurance worth it
atoms.question: Is accident insurance worth it?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare notes that accidents often happen when least expected, and while medical insurance may cover some related costs, extra expenses can add up and lead to financial strain. With accident insurance, the cash benefit payout can help pay for these expenses. The page points to a savings survey as context for why extra cash can matter.

Is it worth buying accident insurance?

atoms.title: Share of adults without emergency savings
atoms.question: How many U.S. adults lack emergency savings?
atoms.text: According to Bankrate's 2023 annual emergency savings report, cited by UnitedHealthcare, 22% of U.S. adults claim they have no emergency savings and 57% are not comfortable with what they have for emergency savings. UnitedHealthcare uses this to show why a cash benefit payout from accident insurance can help when extra expenses add up.

atoms.title: Accident cash benefits can be spent as you choose
atoms.question: How can I use an accident insurance cash benefit?
atoms.text: With an accident insurance plan, the policyholder decides how to use the cash benefit. The page lists expense categories that the benefit can help pay for, and notes the benefit is paid in a stated amount regardless of the actual expense incurred.
questions: What can I spend an accident insurance payout on?
Does accident insurance pay a set amount?

atoms.title: Services an accident plan can help cover
atoms.question: What does an accident insurance plan cover?
atoms.text: An accident insurance plan can help pay for services directly related to an accidental injury, including ambulance service, hospital emergency room care, physical therapy and urgent care center service. Injuries listed include burns, concussions, dislocations, fractures and lacerations. Most services must occur within a certain number of hours and days from the accident, limits may apply, and covered services vary by plan and state.

atoms.title: Accident plans are limited-benefit supplements
atoms.question: Is accident insurance a substitute for health insurance?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare states that accident insurance products provide limited benefits and are supplements to health insurance, not a substitute for the minimum essential coverage required by the Affordable Care Act (ACA). Lack of major medical coverage or other minimum essential coverage may result in an additional payment with taxes. The products pay benefits in a stated amount regardless of the actual expense incurred.

atoms.title: Accident insurance has no network limits
atoms.question: Do I have to use a network with accident insurance?
atoms.text: A footnote on UnitedHealthcare's accident insurance page states there are no network limitations for these accident insurance plans, but a person may be bound to certain networks and providers with their major medical plan.

Can I see any doctor with accident insurance?

atoms.title: Pairing accident insurance with short term plans
atoms.question: Can I add accident insurance to a short term insurance plan?
atoms.text: According to UnitedHealthcare, all products require separate applications, and separate policies or certificates are issued unless the product is a rider or optional benefits. Short term plans have a limited duration, are not renewable, are medically underwritten and do not cover preexisting conditions. They do not meet minimum essential coverage requirements, so signing up may result in a tax penalty, and their expiration does not trigger an ACA special enrollment opportunity.
